chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not make anything of the deeds of the son of Adam greater than fighting in His cause.'
He said: 'And nothing is closer to Paradise than fighting in His cause, and nothing is farther from the Hellfire than fighting in His cause.'
He said: 'And nothing is closer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than fighting in His cause.'
ai.seo_question: What is the greatest deed in the sight of Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to underscore the preeminence of Jihad as the ultimate act of devotion for the Children of Adam, positioning it as the most direct path to Paradise and proximity to Allah. This emphasis reflects the Shia scholarly view of Jihad not merely as warfare but as a comprehensive spiritual and physical struggle that expiates sins and elevates one's rank in the Hereafter. The narration serves to motivate believers by linking the temporal sacrifice of battle directly to eternal reward and divine nearness.
